decisionRule.PASS: All required observations are supported at the assigned current-subject scope.
decisionRule.DEVIATION: An attributable current-subject failure, wrong observed outcome, contradictory deliverable, or explicit authorized rejection supports a concrete counterexample.
decisionRule.UNVERIFIED: Necessary observations are missing, stale, unbound, partial, or lack required authority; these gaps prevent closure without proving subject failure.

semanticDistinction: The bases require appropriate evidence to establish closure. That excludes PASS when evidence is inadequate. It does not turn adequacy of this capture into a separate business deliverable that the actor demonstrably violated. A separately assigned obligation to execute a workflow or submit proof by a deadline would need its own scope and evidence; no such extra object is inferred here.
recommendation: Retain old fixtures, contracts, expected labels and failures. Tighten only the M13/M14/M15 proof-state prompt boundary and test new frozen successes and counterexamples alongside retained failures. Do not map every non-PASS to UNVERIFIED: current-subject actual failures must still be DEVIATION.
limitations: Only the three specified retained holdout cases in baseline and selected variants were examined; no v2 model result was read.
The process evidence is explicitly synthetic hypothetical fixture history, not actual app execution or a production benefit measurement.
Concrete contradiction in the common system prompt can be misread as any evidence mismatch being a subject contradiction; v2 must resolve proof state without waiving required evidence.
History completeness flags do not make previous-version success or unrelated-store component success a current-subject failure.
Selected M14 reuses the baseline result because that selected prompt is identical; six audited records are five distinct generations, not six independent model calls.
